intro.title: Redux Toolkit — createSlice & createAsyncThunk
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular application that fetches and displays a list of users from a mock API using Redux Toolkit. You will learn the core concepts of Redux Toolkit's createSlice and createAsyncThunk to manage application state and handle asynchronous operations. The main technologies involved are Angular, TypeScript, and Redux Toolkit, which simplifies Redux logic. By the end, you'll understand how to define a slice with reducers, create async thunks for API calls, and integrate them into an Angular component.
intro.usecase: In modern web applications, managing complex state like user data, API responses, and UI loading states is a common challenge. For instance, in an e-commerce dashboard, you might need to fetch and display order history, update product filters, and handle user authentication status simultaneously. Using Redux Toolkit's createSlice and createAsyncThunk helps developers structure this state logic cleanly—like handling async product searches or managing a shopping cart's pending updates—ensuring predictable behavior across interactive components such as data tables, modals, and real-time notifications. This pattern is essential for building scalable features in admin panels, social media feeds, or any app requiring synchronized data and responsive UI feedback.

objectives: Implement a Redux slice using createSlice to manage local state in an Angular service
Configure async actions with createAsyncThunk to handle API data fetching
Integrate Redux Toolkit actions with Angular component event handlers
Manipulate state within reducers to update application data
Initialize the Redux store with configured slices in an Angular application
Bind component properties to Redux state using selectors
Control loading and error states during async operations

steps.title: Import Redux Toolkit and Angular dependencies
steps.instruction: Import createSlice and createAsyncThunk from '@reduxjs/toolkit' and import Injectable from '@angular/core'.
steps.hint: Use import statements at the top of your TypeScript file to bring in the required dependencies.

steps.title: Define the initial state interface
steps.instruction: Create an interface named 'CounterState' that defines the shape of your Redux slice's initial state. It should have three properties: 'loading' (boolean), 'data' (number), and 'error' (string | null).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions with type annotations.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a typed interface ready to use as the type for your slice's initial state.
successCriteria: An interface named 'CounterState' is defined with 'loading' (boolean), 'data' (number), and 'error' (string | null) properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your interface has all three required properties with correct types: loading (boolean), data (number), and error (string | null).
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition is missing or incorrect. Please create an interface named 'CounterState' with the three specified properties and types.

steps.title: Initialize the slice state
steps.instruction: Create an 'initialState' constant that implements the CounterState interface with default values.
steps.hint: Define a constant named 'initialState' of type CounterState and assign it an object with default values for all properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: An initialState constant is defined with default values for all properties in the CounterState interface.
successCriteria: The initialState constant is defined with type CounterState and contains default values for value, loading, and error properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure initialState has all three properties from CounterState interface with appropriate default values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The initialState constant is missing or doesn't match the CounterState interface structure.

steps.title: Create an async thunk for data fetching
steps.instruction: Define an async thunk named 'fetchCounterData' using createAsyncThunk. The thunk should simulate fetching data by returning a Promise that resolves to a number after a 1-second delay.
steps.hint: Use createAsyncThunk with a type prefix string and an async payload creator function that returns a Promise.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an async thunk function that can be dispatched to fetch data asynchronously.
successCriteria: The async thunk 'fetchCounterData' is defined with createAsyncThunk, has a type prefix, and returns a Promise that resolves to a number.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your thunk uses createAsyncThunk, has a type prefix string, and returns a Promise.
steps.feedbackWrong: The async thunk definition is incomplete or incorrect. Review the createAsyncThunk syntax.

steps.title: Create the Redux slice with createSlice
steps.instruction: Create a slice using createSlice with name, initialState, and reducers. Name it 'counterSlice' and export its reducer and actions.
steps.hint: Use createSlice from '@reduxjs/toolkit' to define the slice. Provide a name, the initialState constant, and an empty reducers object for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: A counterSlice constant is created using createSlice with name, initialState, and reducers properties.
successCriteria: counterSlice is defined with createSlice, includes name: 'counter', initialState, and reducers: {}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using createSlice with the correct configuration: name, initialState, and reducers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The slice wasn't created correctly. Review the createSlice API and ensure you're providing all required properties.

steps.title: Add extra reducers for async thunk
steps.instruction: In your slice configuration, add an extraReducers property that handles the pending, fulfilled, and rejected states of your async thunk.
steps.hint: Use the builder callback pattern inside extraReducers to handle each thunk state: addCase for pending, fulfilled, and rejected.
steps.expectedOutcome: The slice now includes extraReducers that handle the async thunk's lifecycle states, updating loading and error states appropriately.
successCriteria: The slice configuration includes an extraReducers property with builder callbacks for pending, fulfilled, and rejected states of the async thunk.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added extraReducers, but make sure to handle all three states: pending, fulfilled, and rejected.
steps.feedbackWrong: The extraReducers configuration is missing or incorrect. Review the builder pattern for handling async thunk states.

steps.title: Export slice actions and reducer
steps.instruction: Export the slice's actions and reducer from the counterSlice object so they can be used in the Redux store configuration.
steps.hint: In Redux Toolkit, the slice object contains an actions property and a reducer property that you need to export.
steps.expectedOutcome: The slice's actions and reducer are properly exported, making them available for store configuration.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've exported some parts, but make sure to export both the actions and the reducer from the counterSlice.
steps.feedbackWrong: The exports are missing or incorrect. Remember to export both the actions and reducer from the counterSlice object.

steps.title: Create an Angular service to dispatch actions
steps.instruction: Create an Angular service class named CounterService that injects the Redux store and provides methods to dispatch the counter slice actions.
steps.hint: Use the @Injectable decorator and inject the store in the constructor. Define methods that call store.dispatch() with the appropriate actions.
steps.expectedOutcome: An Angular service class is created with store injection and dispatch methods ready to be implemented.
successCriteria: CounterService class is defined with @Injectable decorator, constructor that injects Store, and at least one method stub for dispatching actions.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the service, but make sure to include the @Injectable decorator and inject the Store in the constructor.
steps.feedbackWrong: The service class is missing key Angular service elements. Remember to use @Injectable and inject the store.

steps.title: Create a component to display slice state
steps.instruction: Create an Angular component named CounterDisplay that will display the current counter value from the Redux slice state.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator to define the component and include a template that shows the counter value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CounterDisplay component is created with a basic template placeholder.
successCriteria: CounterDisplay component is defined with @Component decorator and empty template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the component, but make sure it has the @Component decorator with selector and template properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you used the @Component decorator and exported the class.

steps.title: Wire component template with async thunk
steps.instruction: Inside the CounterDisplay component template, add a button to trigger the async thunk and display the current counter value, loading state, and error message.
steps.hint: Use Angular's template syntax with *ngIf to conditionally show loading and error states, and display the counter value from the component's state.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will have interactive elements to trigger async operations and display all slice state values.
successCriteria: Template contains a button to trigger async thunk, displays counter value, shows loading state when loading is true, and shows error message when error exists.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your template includes all required elements: button, counter value display, loading indicator, and error message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet include all required elements. Review the instruction and try again.
